existing_capabilities: ONC RPC/TCP with record-marking + bounded XDR cursor

missing_capabilities.name: MOUNTPROC_MNT (proc 1) mount attempt + filehandle capture
missing_capabilities.description: RFC 1813 sec 5.2.1. Never issues MNT, so cannot prove mountability, cannot obtain root filehandle for NFSv3 chain, cannot test root_squash. This is the primitive that separates 'showmount says *' from 'I hold /'.

missing_capabilities.name: NFSv3 GETATTR/READDIR/READDIRPLUS/LOOKUP/READ (procs 1/16/17/3/6)
missing_capabilities.description: With handle from MNT, READDIR + GETATTR enumerates tree, owners (UIDs), modes, sizes without a mount() syscall. GETATTR of /root/.ssh or /etc/shadow returning UID=0 world-r is a critical finding. Owner UIDs feed known_users.

missing_capabilities.name: NFSv4 (bound to 2049 directly, no portmap) COMPOUND{PUTROOTFH,GETATTR,READDIR}
missing_capabilities.description: Ganesha and modern Linux nfsd frequently ship NFSv4-only with 111 firewalled. probe() short-circuits when portmap DUMP is empty. NFSv4 pseudo-fs enumeration yields every export without mountd at all. Whole-class blind spot.

missing_capabilities.name: AUTH_UNIX credential (spoof UID for squash policy tests)
missing_capabilities.description: Hard-coded AUTH_NULL cred+verf. Cannot test all_squash/root_squash policy, cannot present spoofed UIDs — the entire 'mount as UID 0/1000' attack requires AUTH_UNIX. Narrative already talks about no_root_squash but tool cannot verify.

missing_capabilities.name: rpcbind v3/v4 DUMP (universal-address form)
missing_capabilities.description: Only PMAP v2 is spoken. v3/v4 uaddr strings reveal the bind interface (0.0.0.0 vs a specific one) which materially changes exposure classification. Modern rpcbind can be configured to hide from v2.

missing_capabilities.name: MOUNTPROC_DUMP (proc 2) — showmount -a — client list
missing_capabilities.description: Returns currently-mounted client hostnames/IPs. Directly feeds hostnames/known_hosts and relay_targets for lateral movement. One RPC, huge recon value.

missing_capabilities.name: NIS/ypserv (RPC 100004) explicit detection + passwd map hooks
missing_capabilities.description: If portmap DUMP lists ypserv, ypcat passwd.byname yields /etc/passwd hashes. Currently swallowed into generic nfs_rpc low. Should be its own high finding and feed known_users + hashes cross-service.

missing_capabilities.name: rpc.statd (100024) / nlockmgr (100021) / rquotad (100011) explicit detection
missing_capabilities.description: Long CVE tail (CVE-2000-0666 statd fmtstr, multiple lockd DoS). Currently swallowed into nfs_rpc; should be per-program findings so CVE mapping can attach.

missing_capabilities.name: UDP portmap DUMP (UDP/111)
missing_capabilities.description: TCP-only today. Misses UDP-only portmap hosts and the reflection/amplification advisory (portmap DUMP amp).
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 1057 App A / CVE-2015-8779-era portmap reflection

missing_capabilities.name: PMAPPROC_CALLIT (proc 5) filter-bypass probe
missing_capabilities.description: Portmapper forwards arbitrary RPCs from its source port, bypassing ACLs that only permit 111. Historic bypass primitive; not tested/flagged.

missing_capabilities.name: NFS server implementation fingerprint
missing_capabilities.description: Linux knfsd vs NFS-Ganesha vs Solaris/Illumos vs BSD nfsd vs NetApp differ on GETATTR/FSINFO edge cases and unhandled procs. Drives CVE mapping (Ganesha CVE-2020-10753 / CVE-2023-34320, knfsd CVE-2022-24448, CVE-2017-7895 short-RPC OOB read, rpcbind CVE-2017-8779 rpcbomb, CVE-2018-5729).

missing_capabilities.name: NFSv4 owner@domain idmap disclosure
missing_capabilities.description: GETATTR of fattr4_owner returns 'user@domain' — reveals AD/Kerberos realm or NFSv4 domain even when no other service leaks it. Zero-cost domain discovery.

missing_capabilities.name: Reserved-port / 'insecure' export flag probe
missing_capabilities.description: Some servers accept non-privileged source ports (multi-tenant / container escape primitive). Testable by MNT from high source port vs reserved.

missing_capabilities.name: Filehandle predictability / cross-export guessing
missing_capabilities.description: Old Linux and some appliances derive fh from (dev,ino,gen) predictably — a handle from one export can be mutated to reach unexported ones.

missing_capabilities.name: Persistent-socket RPC session (chain multiple procs on one TCP)
missing_capabilities.description: Every op opens a fresh TCP. Additions above (MNT + READDIR + NFSv4 COMPOUND) need a session pattern to stay within budget.

cross_service_wire_gaps: known_users <- NFSv3/v4 GETATTR owner UIDs (G2) and NIS passwd map (G7)
hashes <- ypserv passwd.byname when NIS registered (G7)
filehandles / open_shares <- MNT root fh corpus for chain steps (G1)
relay_targets <- mounted client IPs from showmount -a (G6)
priority_gaps: G1 MOUNTPROC_MNT — root fh capture, proves mountability, unlocks NFSv3 chain
G2 NFSv3 READDIR/GETATTR/READ — actual content + owner-UID leak, root_squash proof
G3 NFSv4 COMPOUND on 2049 — entire NFSv4-only host class currently invisible
G4 AUTH_UNIX credential — required to validate the module's own root_squash narrative
G6 MOUNTPROC_DUMP — one RPC, feeds known_hosts + relay_targets cross-service
G7 NIS/ypserv passwd map — feeds known_users + hashes
summary: Module speaks portmap v2 DUMP/GETPORT + mountd EXPORT over TCP only with AUTH_NULL and stops there. It never issues MNT (no filehandle, no root_squash proof), never speaks NFSv3 ops, never speaks NFSv4 (misses every NFSv4-only host since NFSv4 skips portmap), never uses AUTH_UNIX, never reads MOUNTPROC_DUMP client lists, and lumps ypserv/statd/lockd/rquotad into a single low finding — losing high-value cross-service feeds (known_hosts, known_users, hashes, domains, filehandles). No implementation fingerprint, so recent NFS-Ganesha/knfsd/rpcbind CVEs cannot be mapped. No tests exist for the module itself.
notes: Audit only — no code changes. No tests/test_nfs*.py exists; test corpora mention 'nfs' only in generic pipeline/CWE/mock fixtures.
